html:
SMTO-EXE-0084 — The clipboard action took too long and was stopped

GUID: a6d3f783-06b2-550a-905a-8660c987f5c3
Slug: clipboard-timeout
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: clipboard

What happened

  • The Gateway computer didn't finish the clipboard step within its 5-second limit, so SMTO gave up before changing the clipboard.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the Gateway computer is awake, unlocked and not overloaded, with someone signed in at its screen. A sleeping, locked or very busy desktop can keep the clipboard from answering in time.
  2. If the content was copied from an app that is frozen or still loading, wait for that app to respond or close it. Some apps hand over clipboard content only when asked, and a stuck app makes the request run out of time.
  3. Paste on that computer to see what the clipboard holds, then ask SMTO again only if it isn't what you wanted. This confirms the clipboard's state before you send a new request.

What success looks like

  • A new clipboard request finishes within a few seconds and pasting shows the expected content.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Don't include clipboard contents in the report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A clipboard checkpoint reached the 5-second operation deadline while waiting for a native step or the isolated worker; a possibly started write is reported separately as outcome unknown.

What this means

  • A clipboard checkpoint reached its deadline while waiting for a native step or worker result; isolated mutation uncertainty is retained separately. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • A clipboard checkpoint reached its deadline while waiting for a native step or worker result; isolated mutation uncertainty is retained separately.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original operation, clipboard holder/session and effect flags before deciding whether a new request is needed.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway's desktop session (signed in, unlocked, interactive) and whether another application holds the clipboard or is slow to supply delayed-rendered content. Confirm the timed-out request is settled (clipboard.inspect on the same Gateway) before issuing a deliberate new request.
  • Inspect the original operation and session/holder state; reconcile a possibly started write before any new mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Check the desktop session and clipboard owner, then make a deliberate new request if needed.

How to verify the fix

  • The timed-out request and any possible write are settled before further explicit clipboard work.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain clipboard write or include content in diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
